HMMA 5001.title: Fundamentals of Chinese Culture
HMMA 5001.description: This is an integrated multidisciplinary course on Chinese culture, aiming to provide students with a broad understanding of the perspectives and methodologies of humanistic studies on Chinese culture across various disciplines, including history, anthropology, literature, linguistics, philosophy and religion. Emphasis will be put on the introduction of fundamental concepts and general methodological/theoretical underpinnings of the studies of Chinese culture in humanities perspective. This is a compulsory foundation course for all students in the MA program in Chinese Culture.
cilos: Define the nature, scope and values of the studies of Chinese culture in humanities perspectives.
Recognize the basic concepts, theories and methods in different humanities disciplines essential to the building of a holistic, dynamic and integrated understanding of Chinese culture.
Respond critically to Chinese cultural texts and issues of various nature.
Strengthen skills in humanistic inquiry pertaining to Chinese culture, such as questioning, analyzing, interpreting, making connections and constructing arguments.

HMMA 5002.title: Chinese Phonetics and Phonology
HMMA 5002.description: This course is an introduction to the study of sounds in Mandarin Chinese. The course will cover fundamental concepts in phonetics and phonology and compare the sounds of Mandarin with those of other languages. Other topics include: methodology, the typology, learning and evolution of sounds, the subgrouping of Chinese dialects, etc.
cilos: Describe the characteristics of sounds in Mandarin and by extension to other languages with the learnt concepts.
Apply various methods to the study of sounds in languages.
Identify the rules governing sound change in languages.

HMMA 5003.title: Chinese Literary History
HMMA 5003.description: This course aims at familiarizing students with the history of Chinese literature from literary, historical and theoretical perspectives. Emphasis is on the recent scholarship of major genres in Chinese literary history and their interactions in the context of cultural tradition.
cilos: Identify, explain and use cultural concepts and literary theories.
Analyze significant literary phenomena and texts.
Analyze Chinese literature and culture in a global and cross-cultural comparative perspective based on the knowledge and skills of the Humanities from the program.
Conduct original cultural research and participate effectively in project teams using an enhanced knowledge of Chinese literature gained from the course.

HMMA 5005.title: Modern Chinese History
HMMA 5005.description: This course aims at exploring the political and social history of late Imperial and modern China from the 1800s to early 1940s. A selection of important political events and social phenomena are examined to broaden our knowledge of the late-Qing and Republican politics, society and economy as well as revealing the complexity of historical reality in this period.
cilos: Identify and understand the post-modernist discourse of historical narrative.
Deconstruct the different historiographical traditions in official Chinese history in late-imperial and modern periods.
Understand and describe how political persuasions are implanted into official/semi-official narratives of modern historical events.

Analyze critically important political events such as the Opium War, Taiping Movement, Western invasion of China, warlordism, the emergence of Chinese nationalism, developments during the Nanjing Decade, the rise of the Chinese Communist Party, etc.
Learn and apply the skills of presenting one's arguments in academic seminars and the techniques of writing a history paper properly.

HMMA 5006.title: Anthropological Studies of China
HMMA 5006.description: Anthropological consideration of Chinese culture and society. Special topics in Chinese anthropological studies, such as kinship, ethnicity, religion, and regional system.
cilos: Identify basic terms, concepts and theories in cultural anthropology about Chinese cultures and societies in ethnographic writings.
Write critical essays on the development of particular topics in anthropological studies of Chinese societies.
Develop appreciation and respect of fieldwork research, cultural diversity and identify the importance of cultural awareness for social interaction in contemporary daily life.

HMMA 5007.title: Fundamentals of Chinese Philosophy
HMMA 5007.description: This course is designed to guide students to in-depth researches into important issues in Chinese philosophy. The subject matter of the course may vary from one year to another depending on the particular interests of the instructors.
cilos: Analyze Chinese philosophy, discovering how Chinese philosophers make sense of the universe in which they live, how they position themselves both as individuals and as members of the society, and what ideals are they committed to, on both personal and societal levels.
Investigate into both the primary and secondary sources fundamental to the study of Chinese philosophy.
Present their point of view and comment on those of others in front of an audience.
Think critically when conducting their research on the subjects they choose and write professionally when delivering their findings.
Evaluate and apply the philosophies they have learnt to reflect upon their own lives and behavior.

HMMA 5008.title: Languages of China: Anthropological and Cognitive Dimensions
HMMA 5008.description: A cross-disciplinary discussion of issues pertaining to social, historical, cultural, and cognitive aspects of languages and dialects of China, approached from perspectives of areal linguistics, linguistic anthropology, and cognitive linguistics.
cilos: Enhance awareness of linguistic and cultural diversity in China.
Explain how language as a complex adaptive system is shaped by sociohistorical, cultural, and cognitive processes.
Identify the structural components of Chinese languages that are determined or influenced by extralinguistic factors.

Apply the core concepts, theories, and methods employed by cognitive-functional linguists and linguistic anthropologists in the analysis of structuring principles of Chinese and non-Han minority languages of
China.
Analyze Chinese languages, particularly their grammars and lexicons, in a cross-linguistic and cross-cultural comparative perspective.

HMMA 5009.title: History and Theory of Comparative Literature
HMMA 5009.description: This course introduces students to the field of Comparative Literature through a variety of readings. It examines the development of the discipline by looking into the major theories and methodologies. Through readings and in-class discussions, we explore the significance of reading literature from comparative perspectives, crossing geographical, temporal, and linguistic boundaries. We also encourage students to examine the key concepts, themes, and debates that have shaped the evolving field of comparative literature.
cilos: Have a clear idea of the emergence and development of Comparative Literature as a discipline.
Analyze critically the issues of comparative literature related to issues such as translation, identity, intertextually, and globalization.
Formulate their own comparative perspective in a research project on literary texts from different cultural traditions.
Read and talk about dense theoretical texts.
Write about a range of cultural texts using the theories examined in this course.

HMMA 5010.title: Traditional Chinese Literary Theory and Criticism
HMMA 5010.description: This course aims to familiarize students with the traditional Chinese theories and criticism of literature; advantages and limitations of the various modes of discourses such as prefaces to books, poetry-talks, poems on poetry, literary anthologies, stray remarks and commentaries.
cilos: Understand the different stages and their features of the development of Chinese literary theories.
Have exposure to current research trends and methodologies.
Conduct preliminary research.

HMMA 5011.title: Chinese Culture in Jin Yong's Novels
HMMA 5011.description: This course explores the rich tapestry of Chinese culture through the lens of Jin Yong's novels, focusing on key themes such as Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism, as well as the author's compassion for all living beings. By engaging with various works by Jin Yong, such as Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils (Tian Long Ba Bu), students will gain insights into the significance of traditional values and their relevance to contemporary life. The course will include focused readings and discussions, allowing for a deeper understanding of how these cultural elements are woven into Jin Yong's storytelling.
cilos: Analyze traditional Chinese philosophies, including Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism, as presented in various works by Jin Yong.
Evaluate the themes and narratives across different novels and their film adaptations through critical reading and discussion.
Synthesize insights on the relevance of traditional values and the author's compassion for all living beings in the context of contemporary individual lives.

HMMA 5012.title: Chinese Culture in Classics
HMMA 5012.description: This course introduces Chinese culture through reading and interpreting ancient Chinese classics from cultural and linguistic perspectives. It examines the works of ancient Chinese scholars such as Confucius, Guan Zi, Zuoqiu Ming, Zengzi and Laozi, etc. to explore the cultural roots of various social phenomena in modern Chinese society. This course aims to guide students in grasping the essence of Chinese culture through reading classical Chinese texts. Understanding culture begins with understanding the language that carries it. Language is not merely a medium of communication or a vehicle for culture; language itself is a fundamental component of culture.
cilos: Analyze and appreciate the works of classical Chinese, especially in terms of their literature innovation, philosophical value and cultural significance.
Demonstrate basic knowledge of the function words and syntax in Classical Chinese.
Identify the fundamental differences in structural devices and lexical/morphological mechanisms between ancient and modern Chinese language.
Apply the basic principles of Classical Chinese in translating Classical Chinese texts into modern Chinese.
Enhance reading and writing ability and oral communication skill in modern Chinese.

HMMA 5300.title: Topics in Premodern Chinese Literature and Culture
HMMA 5300.description: Through classical works and canonical authors, this course introduces to the students important concepts and knowledge in premodern Chinese literature and culture. Some topics explored in this course include authorship, narrative theory, manuscript culture, and book history.
cilos: Have a knowledge of canonical authors and their works in premodern China.
Describe important concepts and trends in premodern Chinese literary and cultural history.
Approach premodern Chinese texts through theoretical and analytical tools.
Support arguments with textual evidence.
Engage with domestic and international scholarly discussions in the study of premodern Chinese literature and culture.

HMMA 6200.title: Independent Study
HMMA 6200.description: For MA(CC) students only. Students are required to conduct an independent study in a designated subject under the supervision of a faculty member. It may require readings, tutorial discussions, and submission of research paper(s). It may be repeated for credit if different topics are studied.
cilos: Examine a specific topic in Chinese Culture.
Read academic articles critically.
Write academic articles effectively.

HMMA 6300.title: Building a Future Career in Chinese Cultural Studies
HMMA 6300.description: In this self-guided, portfolio-based course, students will reflect on their career goals in connection with their program's content. They will create a portfolio that incorporates insights from courses, seminars, and other relevant events attended during their studies. The course culminates in a written reflection. This course is exclusively designed for MA(CC) students, enriching their understanding of potential career paths in the field of Chinese culture. Graded P or F.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the MA(CC) program's curriculum, emphasizing extra-curricular content and learning outcomes, and their relevance to career paths in Chinese cultural studies.
Design a strategic action plan for future careers in the field of Chinese culture, based on insights gained from the reflective process throughout the course.
Evaluate personal strengths and areas for growth in relation to the program's objectives and potential career opportunities in Chinese cultural studies.
